activity_context.topic_title: Solving Quadratic Inequalities Using the Graphical Method

feedback.worked_solution:
To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the numbers to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & \ge 5x+6 \\ {x}^{2}-5x-6 & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y={x}^{2}-5x-6$ lies above the $x$-axis or touches this axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5x-6 & =0 \\ (x+1)(x-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=-1$ and $x=6,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14059052/assets/51c7484f806696105dd570684f8b194d3c1b7fc3ea27d85a1a17f53e6f7d0a64.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
{x}^{2}-5x-6\ge 0,
$$

we look for the part of the parabola that is above the $x$-axis or touches this axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\le -1$ or $x\ge 6.$ 

Using interval notation, we write $x\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [6,\infty ).$
